The next day, the giraffe went back on the road and saw that the seeds had grown into tall green plants. She was very happy to see the plants grow so big and strong. From that day on, the giraffe would scatter seeds on the road every time she went for a walk. 

Soon, the road was filled with tall green plants and it looked very beautiful. All the animals in the forest loved to walk on the road and see the pretty plants. And the giraffe was very proud of what she had done.

One cloudy day, the King wanted to show his crown to all of his people. He decided to put it on top of his head, but when he opened the box the crown was gone! He was very sorry and searched everywhere for it, but couldn't find it.

The King was very sad. He called all of his people together and asked them to help him look for his crown. They searched the castle and the garden, but it was nowhere to be found. At last, they found it hidden in the King's garden.

The King was so happy to see his crown again and decided to keep it extra safe this time. He put it in a special strong box and locked it with a big, shiny key.

The people cheered and thanked the King for taking care of his crown. He said he was sorry for losing it and promised to keep it safe from now on. And so the King and his people lived happily ever after.

She ran away from the field and back to the pond. She was sad and tired. She told her family what happened. They hugged her and told her that they loved her. Her mom looked at the sign and saw that the pony rides were only for older kids. She felt sorry for Lily. She had an idea.

"Listen, Lily. I know a place where you can see a real pony. It's not far from here. Do you want to go?" she asked.

Lily nodded, wiping her tears. She was curious.

Her mom took her to a farm. There, she saw many animals, like cows, sheep, and chickens. But the best thing was a small brown pony in a stable. It had a friendly face and a soft coat.

"Hello, pony," Lily said, as she reached out her hand.

The pony nuzzled her hand and made a gentle noise. Lily smiled.

"This is Nibbles. He's a very kind pony. He likes carrots and apples. Do you want to feed him?" the farmer asked.

Lily nodded again. She took a carrot from the farmer and gave it to Nibbles. He ate it happily.

"Can I pet him?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can. But be gentle and careful. He's a serious pony. He doesn't like loud noises or sudden movements. He might get scared and kick," the farmer warned.

Lily understood. She stroked Nibbles' neck and back. He closed his eyes and enjoyed it.

Lily felt happy. She forgot about her scraped knee and her missed pony ride. She had made a new friend.

She looked at her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I love ponies. And I love you."

They put everything in a basket and went outside. They found a nice spot under a tree and spread a blanket. They opened the jar of red sauce and poured some on their bread and cheese. Then they took a big bite.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Lily cried. "This sauce is hot! It hurts my mouth!"

"Me too! Me too!" Sam said. "It is spicy! I need water!"

They ran to the house and drank some water from the tap. They felt better, but their mouths still burned. They heard a voice behind them.

"What are you doing here?" It was Mom. She looked angry. "Did you take the spicy sauce from the kitchen?"

Lily and Sam nodded. They felt sorry.

"That sauce is not for you. It is for Daddy. He likes spicy food. You don't. You could get sick. You should have asked me first."

Mom gave them a lecture. She told them to be careful with food they did not know. She told them to always ask before they take something. She told them to not forget the rules.

Lily and Sam listened. They said they were sorry. They hugged Mom and said they loved her.

Mom smiled. She said she loved them too. She said they could have some ice cream to cool their mouths. She said they could still have their picnic, but with a different sauce.

Lily and Sam were happy. They thanked Mom and went back to the backyard. They had their picnic and enjoyed their ice cream. They did not forget the spicy sauce. They learned their lesson.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big pile of ash near a bench. She wondered what it was and how it got there.

She asked her mom, "Mom, what is that black stuff?"

Her mom said, "That is ash, Lily. It is what is left after something burns. Sometimes people make a fire in the park to keep warm or cook food, and then they leave the ash behind."

Lily wanted to touch the ash, but her mom said, "No, Lily, don't touch it. It might be hot or dirty. And it is not nice to play with other people's things."

Lily nodded, but she was still curious. She looked around and saw a stick on the ground. She picked it up and walked to the pile of ash. She poked the ash with the stick and saw it move. She liked how it looked and felt. She started to stir the ash with the stick, making patterns and shapes.

She did not see a man coming from behind the bench. He was the one who made the fire and left the ash. He was not happy to see Lily stirring his ash. He shouted, "Hey, kid, what are you doing? Stop messing with my ash!"

Lily was scared and dropped the stick. She ran to her mom and dad, who heard the man and came to see what was wrong. They saw the man and the ash and understood what happened.

They said to the man, "We are sorry, sir. Lily did not know it was your ash. She was just curious and wanted to play. She did not mean to upset you."

The man looked at Lily and saw she was crying. He felt sorry for her and realized he was too harsh. He said, "It's okay, kid. I'm sorry, too. I was just surprised and angry. You can play with the ash if you want. Just be careful and don't burn yourself."

Lily stopped crying and smiled. She said, "Thank you, sir. You are very kind. Can I share the stick with you?"

The man nodded and smiled back. He said, "Sure, kid. You can share the stick with me. And maybe we can make some more shapes and patterns together."

Lily and the man went back to the pile of ash and stirred it with the stick. They had fun and became friends. Lily's mom and dad watched them and were glad. They thought it was a good day at the park.

"Help, help, the dog is chasing us!" Lily cried.

"Run, run, to the house!" Ben shouted.

Lily and Ben nodded, but they were still angry and sad. They got up and walked to their house, leaving the puddle and the dog behind.

They got the wand from their grandma, who said it was a special gift. She told them to only use it for good things, and not to let anyone else see it.

One day, Tom and Lily were playing in their room with the wand. They took turns to say a spell and wave the wand. The wand made their toys move and talk, and their bed turn into a castle. They had a lot of fun, and laughed a lot.

"Can I try a new spell?" Tom asked Lily. "I want to make something big and cool."

"Okay, but be careful," Lily said. "Don't make a mess or a noise. Mom and dad are in the kitchen, and they don't know about the wand. They might get angry if they find out."

Tom nodded, and looked around the room. He saw a picture of a dinosaur on the wall. He liked dinosaurs, and wanted to see one for real. He pointed the wand at the picture, and said, "Dinosaur, come to life!"

The picture glowed, and then a loud roar filled the room. A big, green dinosaur jumped out of the picture, and landed on the floor. It was bigger than Tom and Lily, and had sharp teeth and claws. It looked around, and saw the twins. It growled, and moved towards them.

Tom and Lily were scared, and dropped the wand. They ran to the door, and tried to open it. But it was locked. They had locked it before they started playing, so no one would come in and see the wand. They forgot to unlock it, and now they were trapped with the dinosaur.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "Mom! Dad! There's a dinosaur in our room!"

Mom and dad heard their screams, and ran to their room. They tried to open the door, but it was locked. They heard the dinosaur roar, and saw its shadow under the door. They were shocked, and worried.

"What's going on in there?" mom asked. "How did you get a dinosaur in your room?"

"We used the wand! The magic wand!" Tom and Lily cried. "We said a spell, and it came to life! Please, let us out!"

Mom and dad looked at each other, and didn't understand. They didn't know about the wand, or the magic. They thought the twins were playing a prank, or having a bad dream. They didn't believe them.

"Stop joking, and open the door," dad said. "There's no such thing as a magic wand, or a dinosaur. You're just making up stories. That's not regular, and we don't allow it."

Tom and Lily felt sad, and scared. They wished they had listened to grandma, and used the wand only for good things. They wished they had never said the spell, and made the dinosaur. They wished they could make it go away, and be safe again. They wished mom and dad would believe them, and help them. They wished they could go back to playing with their toys, and having fun. They wished they could be regular again.

The moral of the story is that it's important to check the date on food before you eat it so you don't make a mistake. Being glad and having fun is great, but taking a few extra moments to check for the date can save you from a bad end.

It ran up to it, but the cobweb seemed strange - a different colour, and it seemed to be calling for help!

The mouse couldn't understand why the cobweb needed help, but it decided to move closer. As it crept closer, it saw two spiders. They were trying to separate two pieces of the cobweb. 

The mouse watched them, trying to understand what was happening. Eventually, it plucked up the courage to ask.

"Why are you trying to separate the cobweb?" it squeaked.

The spiders looked at each other and smiled.

"If we can separate the cobweb, it will protect us from the big storm coming. That way our home won't be damaged," they said.

The mouse was still confused, but it helped the spiders separate the cobweb anyway. As soon as the cobweb was separated, the skies seemed to darken, and a huge storm came! But, because the spiders had separated the cobweb, their homes were safe. 

The mouse was happy to have helped, but also a bit silly for not understanding the situation

So he went towards the smell. He found some spicy food and wanted to eat it. But the food belonged to someone else! 

The owner was very mad. He picked up the animal and put him in a box. Then he kept the animal there. The animal couldn't stay in the forest anymore. 

The end.

Ben and Lily were bored. They wanted to play something fun, but they did not know what. They looked around the room and saw a big desk. The desk had many drawers and papers and pens.

"Let's play guess what's in the desk!" Ben said. He was adventurous and liked to explore new things.

"Okay!" Lily agreed. She was curious and liked to guess.

Ben opened a drawer and took out something. He hid it behind his back.

"Guess what I have!" he said.

"Is it a pen?" Lily asked.

"No, it's not a pen. It's something round and shiny and makes a sound."

"Is it a bell?" Lily guessed.

"No, it's not a bell. It's something you can wear and has a number on it."

"Is it a watch?" Lily guessed.

"Yes, it's a watch! You are smart, Lily!" Ben said. He showed her the watch and let her try it on.

"Wow, it's pretty! Can I have a turn?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can have a turn. Let's see what else is in the desk!" Ben said.

They opened another drawer and found something else. They played guess what's in the desk until they heard their mom calling them for lunch.

"Come on, Ben and Lily, it's time to eat!" their mom said.

"Okay, mom, we're coming!" they said.

They put everything back in the desk and ran to the kitchen. They had a lot of fun playing guess what's in the desk. They decided to play it again another day.

One day a penguin was walking high on a mountain. He was so excited to get to the top and so he kept going. Suddenly he heard a voice and stopped. 

It was a little girl. She said, "Please help! I'm trapped. Thank you thank you!"

The penguin was confused but he wanted to help so he started to climb the rocks to get the girl down. After a long time he almost reached her, but suddenly the rocks shifted and the girl started to slip. Quickly the penguin tried to grab her but he was too late. The little girl fell down and was not seen again. 

The penguin sadly looked down and thanked the little girl for trying to help him. He then slowly walked down the mountain.

Tom and Lily wanted to build a big sand castle by the lake. They took their buckets and shovels and ran to the shore. They found a good spot and started to pile up the sand.

"Look, Lily, I made a tower!" Tom said, proud of his work.

"Wow, Tom, that's great! And I made a wall!" Lily said, showing him her part.

They worked hard and had fun. They added more towers and walls and a gate and a flag. They made their sand castle look very nice.

But then they heard a loud splash. A big dog had jumped into the lake and was swimming towards them. The dog saw their sand castle and thought it was a toy. He ran out of the water and started to dig and bite and knock down their sand castle.

"Hey, stop it, dog! That's our sand castle!" Tom shouted, trying to chase him away.

"Go away, dog! You're ruining our work!" Lily cried, holding her bucket.

But the dog was too strong and fast. He destroyed their sand castle in minutes. Tom and Lily were very sad and angry. They had worked so hard and now their sand castle was gone.

They sat on the sand and looked at the mess. They felt like crying.

"I'm sorry, Tom. We can't build another one. I'm too tired," Lily said, rubbing her eyes.

"Me too, Lily. I'm too tired and it's getting late. We have to go home," Tom said, sighing.

They picked up their buckets and shovels and walked back to their parents. They told them what had happened and how they felt.

Their parents hugged them and said, "We're sorry, Tom and Lily. That was a mean dog. He shouldn't have done that. But you know what? You did a great job building your sand castle. You used your imagination and your skills and your teamwork. You should be proud of yourselves. And you can always build another one another day. Maybe next time, you can find a safer place or put a fence around your sand castle. Or you can make friends with the dog and teach him to be nice. There are many ways to solve a problem. The important thing is to not give up and to learn from your mistakes."

Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They felt better and thanked their parents. They learned that building a sand castle was fun and rewarding, but also that things can go wrong sometimes. They learned to be brave and creative and to not let a bad dog ruin their day. They learned that they could always try again and do better. They learned a valuable lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a wise fish who lived in a big pond. One day, the fish saw a big bird flying above the pond. The bird was holding a big fish in its beak. Suddenly, the bird dropped the fish and it split into two pieces. One piece fell into the pond and the other fell on the grass.

The wise fish saw this and knew it was a good chance to get some food. The fish swam quickly to the piece of fish that fell into the pond and ate it all up. The other animals in the pond were amazed at how quick the wise fish was able to get the food.

From that day on, the wise fish became the leader of the pond because it was the smartest and quickest of them all. And whenever a fish split into two, the wise fish was always the first to grab a piece.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck made of steel. Lily has a doll with a fake dress. Tom likes his truck very much. He makes it go vroom vroom on the floor. Lily likes her doll very much. She makes it talk and sing.

"Can I play with your truck, Tom?" Lily asks. She wants to try the steel truck.

"No, you can't. It's mine. Go play with your doll," Tom says. He does not want to share his truck.

"Please, Tom. Just for a little bit. I'll let you play with my doll," Lily says. She thinks the doll is nice.

"No, no, no. I don't want your doll. It's fake. It's not real. My truck is real. It's steel. It's strong," Tom says. He refuses to share his truck.

Lily feels sad. She does not like Tom's words. She thinks he is mean. She picks up her doll and hugs it.

"Fine. I don't want your truck either. It's loud. It's dirty. It's not fun. My doll is fun. It's pretty. It's soft," Lily says. She walks away from Tom.

Tom feels angry. He does not like Lily's words. He thinks she is rude. He pushes his truck harder on the floor.

"See? My truck is the best. It can go fast. It can make noise. It can do anything," Tom says. He tries to show off his truck.

But then, his truck hits a chair. It makes a loud bang. It breaks a wheel. It stops moving.

Tom feels sad. He does not like his truck anymore. He looks at Lily. She is playing with her doll. She is smiling. She is happy.

"Can I play with your doll, Lily?" Tom asks. He wants to try the doll.

Lily looks at Tom. She sees his broken truck. She sees his sad face. She feels sorry for him.

"Okay, Tom. You can play with my doll. But you have to be nice. You have to share. You have to say sorry," Lily says. She gives him her doll.

Tom takes the doll. He feels the fake dress. He hears the doll talk and sing. He feels happy. He smiles.

"Thank you, Lily. I'm sorry. Your doll is nice. It's real. It's fun," Tom says. He shares his doll with Lily.

Lily takes the doll. She feels the soft hair. She sees the pretty eyes. She feels happy. She smiles.

"You're welcome, Tom. Your truck is nice too. It's real. It's strong. Maybe we can fix it," Lily says. She shares her truck with Tom.

Tom and Lily play with their toys together. They are friends. They are happy. The end.

Maria still didn't understand why the vegetable was so spicy. That night, her mom told her a story before bedtime. Maria listened carefully as her mom told her the story of why vegetables should be eaten, even if they are spicy.

The story was about a Squirrel who loved spicy nuts. This squirrel collected all kinds of spicy nuts and ate them in the morning when he woke up. But one day he was very sick and felt weak. He couldn't eat the spicy nuts anymore because they were making him tired.

So the Squirrel went to his friend, the wise Bear, for help. The Bear said that he needed to eat some different types of food that were less spicy, and explained that he would feel much better if he did. 

The Squirrel realized that the Bear was right and that he needed to understand why he should eat different types of food. So he started eating more vegetables and gradually felt better and stronger.

Every day they put him on the top of a tall chair. It was so high, it made Peter feel scared.

One day, something rare happened. A giant bubble appeared in the sky. It was so big and shiny. Peter had never seen anything like it before.

The bubble came down lower and lower and landed right next to Peter. He was so excited! He jumped down from the chair and ran to the bubble.

But Peter's parents were not happy. They shouted at him for being naughty and for jumping down from the top of the chair. They said that it was not safe and that he must be punished.

So, Peter's parents put him back on the top of the chair. Peter was very sad but he knew he had been naughty and had to be punished. He stayed on the chair until the bubble had disappeared.

By the end of the day, Peter had learned his lesson. He was much better behaved and he never wanted to be punished again.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play together. One night, they heard a loud noise outside their window. They got out of their bed and looked out. They saw a big, dark shape moving in the garden.

"What is that?" Lily asked, feeling scared.

"I don't know," Tom said, feeling brave. "Maybe it is a bear or a monster."

They grabbed their flashlight and went to the door. They wanted to see the shape better. They opened the door quietly and stepped outside.

The shape was still there, but it was not a bear or a monster. It was their dog, Max. He was digging a hole in the grass. He looked up and saw them. He wagged his tail and barked.

"Max, what are you doing?" Tom asked, feeling relieved.

Max did not answer. He just shrugged and went back to digging.

"Maybe he is looking for a bone or a toy," Lily said, feeling curious.

"Or maybe he is just having fun," Tom said, feeling happy.

They decided to join Max and help him dig. They had a lot of fun together. They forgot about the night and the noise. They were alert and playful. They did not want to go back to bed.

John and Mommy were walking down the street. John saw a house. He ran towards it and said, "Mommy, can I go in?"

Mommy smiled and said, "Okay, let's reverse it."

John was confused. He looked at Mommy, and said, "What's 'reverse' mean?"

Mommy laughed and said, "It means 'to go back'. So if you want to go in the house, you have to walk back to it."

John did as he was told. When he reached the house, he went in and explored. He felt proud of himself for following Mommy's instructions. 

But when he came out, he saw Mommy's face. She looked ashamed. John didn't understand why she was ashamed until he saw the sign on the house: "NO TRESPASSING". 

John felt embarrassed. He didn't want to make Mommy mad, so he said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't know." 

Mommy smiled and said, "It's okay, let's go home now." 

On their way back home, John held Mommy's hand extra tight. He was relieved that she was still smiling.

Tom liked to dig in the dirt. He had a small shovel and a bucket. He looked for shiny things in the dirt. He called them minerals. He wanted to find a big mineral, like a diamond.

One day, he saw something shiny in the dirt. He dug and dug until he pulled it out. It was a big mineral. It was round and smooth and sparkled in the sun. Tom was very happy. He put the mineral in his bucket and ran to show his mom.

But when he got to his mom, she was not happy. She looked at the mineral and said, "Tom, this is not a mineral. This is a glass ball. It is not real. It is a toy. Someone must have left it in the dirt."

Tom was very sad. He felt tricked. He wanted a real mineral, not a toy. He asked his mom, "How can I tell if something is a mineral or a toy?"

His mom said, "Well, there are some ways to tell. For example, minerals are usually hard and heavy. They do not break easily. Toys are usually light and soft. They can break easily. And sometimes, toys have words or pictures on them. Minerals do not."

Tom said, "Oh, I see. Thank you, mom. Can I keep the glass ball anyway? It is still pretty."

His mom said, "Yes, you can keep it. But remember, it is not a regular mineral. It is a special toy. And be careful with it. It can break if you drop it or throw it."

Tom said, "OK, mom. I will be careful. And I will keep digging for real minerals. Maybe I will find a diamond someday."

His mom smiled and hugged him. She said, "Maybe you will, Tom. Maybe you will."

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two coal eyes. They were very happy with their snowman.

But then they saw a big truck coming down the road. The truck was wide and loud. It had a sign that said "Yield". Sara and Ben did not know what that meant. They thought the truck wanted to play with their snowman.

"Hello, truck!" Sara shouted. "Do you like our snowman?"

The truck did not answer. It kept coming closer and closer. Sara and Ben got scared. They ran to their house and hid behind the chimney. The chimney was warm and smoky. They hoped the truck would not hurt their snowman.

The truck stopped in front of their snowman. The driver got out. He was wearing a yellow jacket and a hard hat. He looked at the snowman and smiled.

"What a nice snowman!" he said. "I'm sorry, kids, I didn't mean to scare you. I'm here to fix the power line. The sign means you have to let me pass. It's a safety rule."

Sara and Ben peeked from behind the chimney. They saw the driver take a ladder and a tool box from the truck. He climbed the ladder and started to work on the wire.

"Can we come out?" Sara asked.

"Sure, you can come out. But stay away from the ladder and the wire. They can be dangerous." the driver said.

Sara and Ben came out from behind the chimney. They walked to their snowman and hugged him.

"We're sorry, snowman. We thought the truck was going to smash you." Ben said.

The snowman did not answer. He just smiled with his carrot nose and his coal eyes. He was happy to have Sara and Ben as his friends.

The Lion laughingly said, "Let's try anyway. Ready, set, go!". The Lion started to run but the Turtle didn't move. The Lion stopped and said, "Why aren't you running?" The Turtle answered, "You are much faster than me. I can't win against you no matter how hard I try." The Lion thought for a moment, then smiled. He said, "You don't always have to race to show how fast you are. You can be fast in another way, like this!" The Lion then roared loudly and jumped in the air, showing how mighty and strong he could be. The Turtle liked this idea and said, "Yes, I can be pretty fast too!" He started to roar and jump around in the swamp. The Lion laughed as they skipped around the swamp.

The moral of this story is that there are many ways to be fast and strong without always competing with others. We can be pretty fast by using our brains and showing how brave and clever we can be.

In the end, Timmy learned that it's not good to be selfish and that sometimes fighting isn't the best answer. He wished he had listened to Sally's advice and not tried to fight the mosquito.

Once upon a time, a bird was flying in the sky. He had one special wing. He could use this wing to sign his name. He was very proud of his magic.

The bird was very serious about his skill. He wanted to show everyone how he could sign his name with his wing. So he practiced everyday.

One day, he flew very close to some people. He said to them, "Look at me! I can sign my name with my wing!" But nobody seemed impressed.

The people were angry and said, "We don't care about your skill. Go away or we'll be forced to hurt you!"

The bird was very scared and flew away quickly. But he was so frightened that he forgot to close his wing. The people grabbed his wing and broke it.

The poor bird never flew again. He was forced to walk everywhere and he could never sign his name again.

Then, she saw a little girl in the audience. The girl was wearing a pink dress and pink shoes, just like Sara. But the girl was not happy. She was crying. Sara asked her why she was crying. The girl said that she wanted to be a dancer, but she had hurt her leg and could not dance. She said that she loved to watch the other dancers, but Sara had blocked her view and made them unhappy.

She said that she was sorry and that she wanted to share the dance with them. The other dancers forgave her and welcomed her. They danced together in a circle, with Sara and the girl in the middle. They all shone with joy and friendship.

The moral of the story is that being a good dancer is not only about being bright and beautiful, but also about being kind and respectful. Sharing and caring make everyone happy.

Sam was a little boy who liked to imagine. He imagined he was a superhero, a pirate, a dinosaur, and many other things. He had a lot of fun playing with his toys and making up stories.

One day, his mom asked him to help her in the kitchen. She wanted him to peel an onion for the soup. Sam had never peeled an onion before, so he was curious. He took the onion and started to peel off the skin. But soon, he felt a sting in his eyes and nose. He started to cry and sneeze.

"Mom, what is this? It hurts!" he said, dropping the onion.

"That's an onion, Sam. It has a strong smell that makes your eyes water. But it also makes the soup tasty and healthy. You have to be brave and finish peeling it," his mom said, wiping his tears.

Sam didn't want to peel the onion anymore. He wanted to go back to his room and imagine. He thought the onion was mean and nasty. He said, "I don't like onions. They are bad. I don't want to eat them."

His mom smiled and said, "You know, Sam, sometimes things that seem bad are actually good for you. Onions may make you cry, but they also help you fight germs and stay strong. They are like your friends, even if they don't look or smell nice. You should give them a chance and try them. Maybe you will like them after all."

Sam thought about what his mom said. He decided to be brave and peel the onion again. He still felt the sting, but he didn't cry or sneeze. He finished peeling the onion and gave it to his mom. She thanked him and gave him a hug.

Later, when the soup was ready, Sam tasted it. He was surprised. The soup was delicious and warm. He felt comfortable and happy. He said, "Mom, you were right. The onion is good. It makes the soup yummy. I like onions now. Thank you for teaching me."

His mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Sam. I'm proud of you. You learned a valuable lesson today. You learned to imagine not only what you want, but also what you need. You learned to be open-minded and try new things. You learned to appreciate the good in the bad. That's a very important skill to have in life. Well done, Sam."

Sam smiled and hugged his mom. He felt proud and grateful. He enjoyed the soup and his mom's company. He still liked to imagine, but he also liked to learn. He thought, "Imagining is fun, but learning is fun too. I can do both. I can be a superhero and a good boy."

Sara and Tom were brother and sister. They liked to play in the park with their ball and their bike. One day, they saw a tall man in the park. He had a big bag and a thermometer in his hand. He looked at the trees and the flowers with the thermometer.

"Hello, what are you doing?" Sara asked the tall man.

"I am a scientist. I am measuring how hot or cold the plants are. Do you want to see?" the tall man said.

"Yes, please!" Tom said. He liked to learn new things.

The tall man showed them how the thermometer worked. He put it on a leaf and said, "This leaf is 20 degrees. That means it is warm, but not too hot." He put it on a flower and said, "This flower is 15 degrees. That means it is cooler than the leaf." He put it on a rock and said, "This rock is 10 degrees. That means it is cold and hard."

Sara and Tom were amazed. They asked the tall man many questions. He answered them kindly. He told them that plants need the right temperature to grow and be healthy. He also told them that people need the right temperature to be well and happy.

"Thank you for teaching us, Mr. Scientist. You are very smart and nice," Sara said.

"You are welcome, Sara and Tom. You are very curious and polite," the tall man said. "But remember, you should not touch the thermometer without asking. It is a tool, not a toy. It can break or hurt you if you are not careful."

Sara and Tom nodded. They understood. They said goodbye to the tall man and went back to their ball and their bike. They had fun in the park, but they also learned something new. They were glad they met the tall man with the thermometer.

The little girl jumped, then looked at her mom in surprise. "Don't be scared," Mom said, "You were playing a wonderful rhythm - but remember, a broken branch can break more easily than a stick."

And the rhythm continued, stronger and wiser than before.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben said. They heard Mom and Dad coming. They were scared.

Mom and Dad saw the package on the floor. They opened it and saw a beautiful vase that Grandma and Grandpa had sent them. But it was broken into many pieces.

"What happened?" Mom asked. "Who did this?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry. They knew they had done something bad.

"It was me," Ben said. "I wanted to see what was inside. I'm sorry, Mom and Dad. I didn't mean to break it."

Mom and Dad were sad and angry. But they also saw that Ben was honest and brave. They hugged him and Lily.

"Thank you for telling the truth, Ben," Dad said. "But you should not have touched the package. It was not yours. And you should have listened to Lily. She was right. It was delicate and it could break easily. You have to respect other people's things and be careful with them."

"I'm sorry, Dad," Ben said. "I learned my lesson. I will not do it again."

Lily and Ben helped Mom and Dad clean up the mess. They wrote a letter to Grandma and Grandpa to apologize and to thank them for the vase. They hoped they would forgive them.

The moral of the story is: You should not touch things that are not yours and you should be careful with delicate things. You should also listen to your siblings and tell the truth when you make a mistake.

Just then, his grandad walked past. Alex told grandad about the big fish, and grandad said he knew where to get a rod. He took Alex to the shop, and together they bought a large rod that was perfect for fishing.

Alex raced back to the river, fishing rod in hand. He was so excited, he didn't even worry if he would catch the big fish. That day, Alex caught the biggest fish in the river!

One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Leo, and he had no toys. He saw Sara and Ben playing with the ball, and he wanted to join them. He asked them nicely, "Can I play with you and your ball?"

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They did not want to share their ball. They liked it too much. They said to Leo, "No, you can't. This is our ball. Go away."

Leo felt sad and lonely. He had no friends and no toys. He walked away, but he did not give up. He was persistent. He came back the next day, and the next, and the next. He always asked the same question, "Can I play with you and your ball?"

Sara and Ben always said the same answer, "No, you can't. This is our ball. Go away."

But then, they saw Leo. He was on the other side of the street. He saw the ball and the car too. He ran fast, faster than the car. He grabbed the ball and saved it. He threw it back to Sara and Ben, over the fence, into the yard.

Sara and Ben were happy. They got their ball back. They thanked Leo. They said, "You are brave and kind. You saved our ball. We are sorry we were mean to you. Can you play with us and our ball?"

Leo smiled. He said, "Yes, I can. I would love to play with you and your ball."

Sara and Ben learned a lesson. They learned to value their toys, but also to value their friends. They learned to share and be nice. They played with Leo and their ball every season, and they had more fun than ever.

Anna liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and fuzzy. Anna wanted to touch it.

"Hello, caterpillar," Anna said. "Can I be your friend?"

The caterpillar did not say anything. It curled up into a ball. It was shy. It did not like to talk to strangers.

Anna felt sad. She wanted to make the caterpillar happy. She thought of an idea. She ran to the house and got a small box. She put some leaves and grass in the box. She gently picked up the caterpillar and put it in the box.

"Look, caterpillar," Anna said. "I made you a home. You can eat and sleep here. You will be safe and warm. I will lock the box so no one can bother you."

The caterpillar looked at Anna. It saw that she was kind and gentle. It uncurled a little bit. It nibbled on a leaf. It felt a bit better.

"Thank you, Anna," the caterpillar said. "You are a good friend. But I don't need to stay in the box. I need to make a cocoon. Then I will become a butterfly. I will fly and see the world. And I will come back and visit you."

Anna was surprised. She did not know that caterpillars could become butterflies. She was happy for the caterpillar. She opened the box and let it out.

"Wow, caterpillar," Anna said. "That is amazing. I can't wait to see you as a butterfly. You will be beautiful and brave. I will miss you, but I will always be your friend."

The caterpillar smiled. It crawled to a branch and started to spin a cocoon. It was not shy anymore. It was ready for a change. It thanked Anna again and said goodbye.

Anna watched the caterpillar make its cocoon. She felt proud and curious. She wondered how long it would take. She decided to visit the garden every day and wait for the butterfly. She hoped it would remember her. She hoped it would be happy.

The end.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play with tools. They have a big box of tools. They have hammers, nails, saws, and more.

One day, Tim and Sam are playing with the tools. Tim picks up a hammer. He says, "Look, Sam, I have a hammer. I can hammer anything I want."

Sam says, "No, Tim, you can't hammer anything you want. You can only hammer nails. If you hammer something else, you will break it or hurt it."

Tim says, "No, Sam, I can hammer anything I want. Watch me." He swings the hammer and hits a toy car. The toy car makes a loud noise and falls apart.

Sam is upset. He says, "Tim, that was my toy car. You broke it. That was not nice. That was not a joke. That was mean."

Tim is sorry. He says, "Sam, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to break your toy car. I was trying to joke. I thought it would be funny. But it was not funny. It was bad."

Sam is still upset. He says, "Tim, you have to be careful with the hammer. The hammer is not for joking. The hammer is for hammering nails. You have to ask before you use my toys. You have to be a good friend."

Tim says, "Sam, you are right. I have to be careful with the hammer. I have to ask before I use your toys. I have to be a good friend. Can you forgive me?"

Sam thinks for a moment. He says, "Tim, I forgive you. But you have to help me fix my toy car. And you have to promise not to joke with the hammer again."

Tim says, "Sam, I promise. I will help you fix your toy car. And I will not joke with the hammer again. Thank you for forgiving me."

Tim and Sam hug. They are friends again. They put the hammer back in the box. They find some glue and some tape. They try to fix the toy car. They have fun. They are happy.

But Anna had a big wish. She wanted to see what it was like to be a baby again. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I reverse and be a baby for a day?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Why do you want to do that, Anna? Being a big girl is so much better. You can do many things that babies can't."

Anna said, "But babies are so cute and cuddly. And they don't have to go to school or do chores. I want to try it, please."

Her mom thought for a moment. Then she said, "Okay, Anna. But only for a day. And only if you promise to come back to being a big girl tomorrow. Deal?"

Anna nodded and said, "Deal!"

Her mom took her to the bedroom and gave her a magic bottle. She said, "Drink this, Anna. It will make you reverse and be a baby for a day. But remember, you have to drink it again tomorrow to come back to being a big girl. Don't lose it, okay?"

Anna drank the magic bottle and felt a strange tingling. She looked at her mom and said, "Goo goo gaa gaa."

Her mom picked her up and said, "Oh, Anna. You are a baby now. You are so cute and cuddly. But you can't talk or walk or play with your friends. You can only cry and sleep and eat. Is that what you wanted?"

Anna tried to answer, but she could only make baby noises. She realized that being a baby was not as fun as she thought. She missed her cake, her presents, and her friends. She wanted to be a big girl again.

She looked at the magic bottle in her mom's hand and reached for it. She wanted to drink it and reverse again. But her mom said, "No, Anna. You have to wait until tomorrow. You made a deal, remember? You have to be a baby for a day. Maybe you will learn something interesting from this experience."

Anna cried and cried. She wished she never asked to reverse and be a baby. She learned that being a big girl was much better. She hoped that tomorrow would come soon. She hoped that her birthday would not be ruined by her silly wish.

Lily was a bee who liked to fly very fast. She did not listen to her mom or dad, who told her to be careful and stay close to the hive. She wanted to see everything in the garden and the sky.

One day, she saw a big red flower that smelled very sweet. She flew towards it, but did not see the spider web that was in front of it. She got stuck in the sticky web and could not move. She was scared and cried for help.

"Help me, help me!" she buzzed.

Sam was a bee who was flying nearby. He heard Lily's cry and flew to see what was wrong. He saw her trapped in the web and felt sorry for her.

"Don't worry, Lily, I will help you," he said. He used his strong jaws to cut the web and free Lily. He helped her fly back to the hive.

"Thank you, Sam, you are very kind," Lily said.

"You are welcome, Lily, but you should be more careful. The garden and the sky are full of dangers. You should listen to your mom and dad and stay close to the hive," Sam said.

Lily nodded and said sorry. She learned her lesson and never flew too far or too fast again. She and Sam became good friends and flew together in the garden and the sky, but always close to the hive.

Tom and Lily were making pizza with their mom. They had a big ball of dough to roll and shape. Mom gave them each a piece of dough and a rolling pin.

"Be careful with the dough, children. Don't slap it too hard or it will break," Mom said.

Tom and Lily nodded and started to roll their dough. Tom wanted to make a big pizza, so he rolled his dough very thin. Lily wanted to make a small pizza, so she rolled her dough very thick.

"Look, Mom, my pizza is bigger than Lily's!" Tom said, holding up his dough.

"That's nice, Tom, but you have to leave some space for the sauce and the cheese," Mom said.

Lily looked at Tom's pizza and felt jealous. She wanted a big pizza too. She had an idea. She waited until Tom was not looking and slapped his dough with her hand. Tom's dough tore and made a hole.

"Hey, what did you do?" Tom cried, seeing his dough ruined.

"I slapped your pizza, because I wanted a big pizza too," Lily said, smirking.

"That's not fair, Lily! You ruined my pizza!" Tom said, angry.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom's dough with a hole and Lily's dough with a handprint.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"Lily slapped my pizza and made a hole!" Tom said.

"Is that true, Lily?" Mom asked.

Lily looked down and nodded. She felt ashamed.

"Why did you do that, Lily?" Mom asked.

"Because I was jealous of Tom's pizza," Lily said.

Mom sighed and said, "Lily, that was not a nice thing to do. You should not slap other people's things, because that can hurt them and make them sad. You should be happy with what you have and share with others. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Tom. I was wrong to slap your pizza."

Tom looked at Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. But next time, don't slap my pizza, okay?"

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, Tom. Next time, I will ask you if I can have some of your pizza, okay?"

Tom smiled and said, "Okay, Lily. Next time, I will share some of my pizza with you, okay?"

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, children. Now, let's fix your dough and make some pizza together, okay?"

Tom and Lily nodded and hugged Mom. They learned to be kind and generous with each other. They made some delicious pizza and ate it with Mom. They were happy and full.

The girl had lots of fun playing in the sun, but she always remembered to put on her sun hat and sunscreen so that she was protected from the sun. 

Later, when the girl's mom came to pick her up, she was so proud of her daughter for keeping her promise and taking care of herself in the sun.

The moral of this story is that we should always follow the advice of our parents and protect ourselves from the sun.

Tommy was miserable again. He wished he had listened to his mom. He wished he had his boots and raincoat. He wished he could go back to the puddle. He cried and hugged his teddy bear. He hoped his mom would forgive him. He hoped it would stop raining soon.

"No, they are mine. I want them. You can have the tuna," he said.

"What are you doing?" she asked.

"We were trying to make lunch," Anna said.

"But we couldn't agree on what to eat," Ben said.

She ran to the gate. She grabbed a bar. She pulled herself up. She felt happy and brave. She climbed higher and higher. She looked around. She saw the trees, the flowers, the birds. She saw the swings, the slide, the sandbox. She saw her mom. Her mom was talking to another mom. Her mom did not see her.

She climbed higher and higher. She reached the top. She smiled. She felt proud. She waved to the birds. She did not see the sign. The sign said "Danger. High Voltage. Do Not Touch." She did not know what it meant. She touched the wire. The wire was hot. The wire was angry. The wire hurt her. She screamed. She fell. She did not climb anymore.

"Look what happened", Mary said, pointing at an old, ugly snake outside the window!

"Oh no, don't worry Mary", said Lisa, giving her a big hug. "We can fix this, I'm sure".

That's exactly what they did. Some of the other pupils helped too and soon enough the window was fixed.

Lisa and Mary gave each other a big high five. The snake had been sent away and they were all safe and happy.

Lisa felt happy that everyone had come together to fix the broken window. It felt like they were all one big family.

The mommy bunny decided to use all of their family's money to buy some food for the daddy bunny. The little bunny wanted to help so he decided to tell his mommy bunny about something he saw in the forest.

In the forest, he saw a tree full of delicious, healthy fruit. The bunny told his mommy that if she could find the tree, she could get their family the healthy food that they needed. 

The mommy bunny found the tree and was able to bring back enough food to support her family. Daddy bunny soon began to feel better, and the bunny family ate happy and healthy meals every night. 

The little bunny's courageous decision to tell his mommy bunny about the tree's fruit taught him that even small efforts to help others can make a big difference in their lives.

"Maybe it has candy or a new toy," Lily said.

"Or maybe it has a monster or a spider," Ben said.

They opened the box and saw a lot of old clothes and books. They were not happy.

"This is not fair," Lily said. "Who put this here?"

"Maybe it was Mom or Dad," Ben said. "They always give us old things."

They decided to make a fort with the clothes and books. They put some on the ground and some on top. They made a door and a window. They crawled inside and pretended they were in a castle.

"This is fun," Lily said. "We can provide for ourselves."

"Yes, we can," Ben said. "We don't need anyone else."

They played for a long time until they heard a voice outside.

"Hello, children," the voice said. "Do you like the box?"

They peeked out and saw a lady with a big smile. She had a badge that said "Charity".

"I'm sorry to bother you, but I'm here to pick up the box. It belongs to the charity. We provide clothes and books for people who need them."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They did not know the box was for charity. They thought it was for them.

"Sorry, lady," Lily said. "We did not know. We thought it was ours."

"That's okay, children," the lady said. "You can keep some of the clothes and books if you want. But please give the rest to me. There are many people who would be happy to have them."

Lily and Ben nodded. They gave the lady most of the clothes and books. They kept a few for themselves. They thanked the lady and said goodbye.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that some things are not fair, but some things are. They learned that it is good to provide for others, not just for themselves. They learned that they can still have fun with what they have.

They hugged each other and smiled. They were still best friends.

What is self-attention?
<|assistant|>
Self-attention allows each token in a sequence to consider other
tokens when creating its representation. Query, key, and value
vectors are used to calculate attention relationships.
<|end|>

He pretended to be sad and asked the rabbit if he could play with the ball for just a little while. The rabbit felt sorry for the prince and gave him the ball. 

The prince was so happy! He thanked the rabbit and rolled his ball all the way back to the castle. From then on, the prince made sure to keep a close eye on his ball so it wouldn't roll away again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a bird who was feeling very brave. He wanted to explore the world around him, but he was a little afraid. He stood at the edge of a cliff and looked down. Then he took a deep breath and spread his wings. He started to soar up over the trees and away from the cliff.

The bird felt so free and happy as the breeze blew through his feathers and the clouds whisked past. He twirled and spun in the sky, sometimes even flying upside down. Suddenly he heard a whistle coming from below. He looked down and saw a little boy standing in a field, looking up at him with a big smile on his face.

The bird was a bit frightened, so he stopped flying and just hovered in the sky. The little boy kept whistling, and soon the bird started to slowly float towards the ground. When he was close enough, the little boy reached out and touched the bird's wings.

The bird was so surprised, but he wasn't scared anymore. He flapped his wings and began soaring through the sky again. He flew over trees and rivers and mountains, and he felt so happy that he could fly. The little bird had discovered a new kind of freedom, and he never forgot his first adventure.

Sam feels hurt. He likes his boat. It is blue and shiny and makes a nice sound. He does not want to play with Tom anymore.

"Can I try your boat?" Sam asks Tom.

"No, you can't!" Tom says. "It is my boat. You might break it or lose it. Go away!"

Sam goes away. He feels sad and angry. He thinks Tom is mean and rude.

The next day, Tom goes to the pond with his boat. He sees Sam there. Sam has a new friend. His name is Ben. Ben has a boat too. It is green and bright and has a sail.

"Hi, Sam!" Ben says. "Do you want to race our boats?"

"Yes, I do!" Sam says. "That sounds fun!"

They put their boats in the water and make them go fast. They laugh and cheer.

Tom feels lonely. He wants to play with them. He thinks their boats are nice too.

"Can I play with you?" Tom asks Sam and Ben.

Sam and Ben look at Tom. They remember how he was mean to Sam.

"No, you can't!" Sam says. "You were not nice to me. You did not share your boat. You made me feel hurt. Go away!"

Tom goes away. He feels sad and sorry. He thinks he was mean and rude.

He learns a lesson. He learns that if he wants to have friends, he has to be kind and share. He learns that being hurt is not good. He learns that being nice is better. He decides to say sorry to Sam and invite him to play with his boat. He hopes Sam will forgive him and be his friend again.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and find things. Sometimes they found shells, or rocks, or coins. They put them in their buckets and showed them to each other.

One day, Lily noticed something shiny in the sand. She dug it out with her hands and held it up. It was a small, clear stone that sparkled in the sun. "Look, Max, I found a diamond!" she said.

Max looked at the stone and frowned. He did not think it was a diamond. He thought it was a piece of glass. He had seen glass before, and it looked like that. "That's not a diamond, Lily. That's glass. Diamonds are colorful, like rainbows. My mom has a diamond ring, and it has many colors."

Lily did not believe Max. She thought he was jealous of her find. She put the stone in her pocket and said, "No, it's a diamond. I know it is. It's the most beautiful thing I ever saw. You're just mean, Max."

Max felt hurt by Lily's words. He did not want to fight with her. He wanted to play with her. He decided to show her his mom's ring and prove that he was right. He said, "Come on, Lily. Let's go to my house. I'll show you my mom's ring. Then you'll see what a real diamond looks like."

Lily agreed to go with Max. She was curious to see his mom's ring. She hoped it was not as pretty as her stone. She did not want to admit that she was wrong. She followed Max to his house, still holding the stone in her pocket. She did not know that the stone was not a glass or a diamond, but a very rare and valuable gem that someone had lost in the park. She did not know that someone was looking for it, and would soon find out where it was. She did not know that her stone would cause a lot of trouble for her and Max. She only knew that she liked it, and that it was hers.

So, they started to balance on one leg. The friend fell down first, but the truck kept balancing. The truck was very good at balancing because it was big and strong.

After the game, the truck said, "That was fun! Let's play again sometime." The friend agreed and they drove away together. The end.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big swing. Lily wants to swing high. Tom wants to swing low.

"Can I swing first?" Lily asks.

"OK, but only for a little bit," Tom says.

Lily gets on the swing. She pushes with her feet. She swings high and fast. She feels the wind in her hair. She laughs.

"Wow, you are so good at swinging!" Tom says.

"Thank you, Tom. Do you want to try?" Lily asks.

Tom nods. He gets on the swing. He does not push with his feet. He swings low and slow. He feels bored.

"This is not fun," Tom says.

"Why don't you push with your feet?" Lily asks.

"I don't want to. I am lazy," Tom says.

Lily sees something shiny on the ground. She gets off the swing. She runs to the shiny thing. It is an egg.

"Look, Tom, I found an egg!" Lily says.

"Where did it come from?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe a bird left it here," Lily says.

"Can we open it?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe we should leave it alone," Lily says.

"But I want to see what is inside," Tom says.

He gets off the swing. He runs to Lily. He takes the egg from her hand. He tries to crack it.

"Tom, don't do that!" Lily says.

But it is too late. The egg breaks. A baby bird comes out. It is wet and scared. It cries.

"Tom, you hurt the baby bird!" Lily says.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't know," Tom says.

They feel bad. They don't know what to do. They hear a loud noise. They look up. They see a big bird. It is the baby bird's mom. She is angry. She flies to them. She takes the baby bird in her beak. She flies away.

"Bye, baby bird," Lily says.

"Bye, baby bird," Tom says.

They are sad. They are sorry. They hug each other.

"Let's go home," Lily says.

"OK, let's go home," Tom says.

They walk away. They don't play with the swing anymore. They don't play with eggs anymore. They learn a lesson. They are not lazy anymore. They are careful and kind.

"What are those?" their moms asked.

"They are cakes!" Tim and Sam said. "We made them in the mud!"

Their moms shook their heads. They did not like the mud cakes. They did not like the mess. They did not like the smell.

"Those are not cakes, those are dirt!" their moms said. "You need to go to the bath right now! And throw those things away!"

Tim and Sam felt sad. They did not understand why their moms did not like their mud cakes. They thought they were beautiful. They wanted to display them on the table.

"But mom, we worked hard on them!" Tim and Sam said. "They are our gifts for you!"

Their moms sighed. They loved their sons, but they did not love their mud cakes. They hugged them and kissed them on the cheek.

"Thank you for your gifts, but they are not good for the house," their moms said. "You can make other gifts that are clean and nice. Now, go to the bath and wash your waist and your face and your hands and your hair. And don't play in the mud again!"

Tim and Sam nodded. They dropped their mud cakes in the trash and went to the bath. They scrubbed and rinsed and dried. They put on clean clothes and combed their hair. They looked at each other and smiled.

"Maybe we can make paper cakes next time," Tim said.

"Or clay cakes," Sam said.

The cartoon replied, "because there is someone that wants to take me away for themselves. And I can't do anything about it." Mary was really upset, but she said, "I will try to save you! I won't let that bad person take you away!"

But it was too late. The bad person had already taken the cartoon away and there was nothing Mary could do to save it. The cartoon was gone forever, and Mary felt so sad.

Once, there was an old farmer who lived in a big field. Every day he worked very hard planting vegetables, and the vegetables always grew strong and healthy. Everyone in the village said he was a very successful farmer.

When he got home, he was very tired. He looked out over the field and regretted not spending the day tending to his vegetables. He was a successful farmer, but he had wasted the day doing nothing.

The old farmer learnt a valuable lesson that day. He made sure he never wasted an opportunity like that again. Every day he worked hard in his field, and his vegetables kept growing strong and healthy.

The storm went away after a while and the sun came out. The little mouse hugged the lion in thanks and they ran around the jungle, becoming the best of friends. The lion roared with happiness!

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball, a bike and a doll. They share their toys and have fun.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and has a red collar. The dog runs to them and barks. Lily and Ben are scared. They drop their toys and run away.

"Whoa, whoa, whoa!" a voice says. "Don't be afraid. He is friendly. He just wants to say hello."

Lily and Ben stop and look. A man is holding the dog's leash. He smiles at them.

"Hi, I'm Tom. This is Rex. He is my dog. He likes to play, too. He won't hurt you. Do you want to pet him?"

Lily and Ben nod. They walk slowly to the man and the dog. They touch the dog's fur. It is soft and warm. The dog licks their hands. It tickles.

"Good boy, Rex. Good boy." Tom says. "He likes you. You are nice kids."

Lily and Ben giggle. They like Rex, too. He is a good dog.

"Can we play with him?" Lily asks.

"Sure, you can. But only for a little while. It's almost lunch time. We have to go home soon." Tom says.

"Okay. Thank you." Ben says.

They play with Rex. They throw the ball and he fetches it. They ride the bike and he runs after them. They hug the doll and he sniffs it.

They have a lot of fun. They forget about their toys.

"Time to go, kids. Say bye to Rex." Tom says.

"Bye, Rex. We'll miss you." Lily and Ben say.

They wave to Tom and Rex. They walk back to their toys.

But they see something wrong. Their toys are gone. Someone took them.

"Where are our toys?" Lily cries.

"Who took them?" Ben asks.

They look around. They see a boy and a girl. They have their toys. They are playing with them.

"Hey, those are our toys!" Lily shouts.

"Give them back!" Ben yells.

The boy and the girl look at them. They laugh.

"No, they are not. They are ours. We found them. Finders keepers." The boy says.

"That's not fair. You stole them. They belong to us. We were playing with them." The girl says.

"Too bad. We like them. They are ours now. Go away." The girl says.

They stick out their tongues. They run away with the toys.

Lily and Ben are sad and angry. They want their toys back. They don't know what to do.

They hear a bark. They see Rex. He is running to them. He has something in his mouth. It is the ball.

"Rex!" Lily and Ben say.

They hug Rex. He drops the ball. He wags his tail.

"Good boy, Rex. Good boy." Tom says. He is behind Rex. He has something in his hands. It is the bike and the doll.

"Here, kids. I saw what happened. Those kids were mean. They took your toys. But Rex and I got them back. Here you go." Tom says.

He gives them the bike and the doll. They take them.

"Thank you, Tom. Thank you, Rex. You are the best." Lily and Ben say.

They smile. They are happy. They have their toys back.

They play with Tom and Rex. They share their toys. They have more fun.

They hear a bell. It is lunch time. They have to go home.

"Bye, Tom. Bye, Rex. See you soon." Lily and Ben say.

"Bye, kids. Have a good lunch. See you later." Tom says.

They wave to Tom and Rex. They go home with their toys.

They have a sweet lunch. They have sandwiches, apples and cookies. They are yummy.

They think about Tom and Rex. They are their friends. They are nice.

They belong together.

"Look, mom, I found a worm!"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's nice, Lily. But you should be gentle with the worm. It might be fearful of you. Worms like to rest in the dirt, not in your hand."

Lily did not want to scare the worm. She wanted to make it happy. She said, "Sorry, worm. I did not mean to hurt you. You can go back to the dirt and rest."

She put the worm down on the ground and watched it crawl away. She waved and said, "Bye, worm. Maybe I will see you again."

She felt proud of herself for being kind to the worm. She ran to her mom and gave her a hug. Her mom hugged her back and said, "You are a good girl, Lily. I love you."

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom."

Once upon a time there was a nosy little bird called Dug. Dug was always curious and listened to every sound he could hear. One day as Dug was flying around, he suddenly heard a peculiar whistle and became very curious. He wanted to know where it was coming from.

Dug flew all around until he finally found the source of the whistle. He saw it was a little girl, who was blowing a whistle and playing with her friends. Dug watched from a nearby tree, fascinated.

All of a sudden, the girl's father appeared, scaring away Dug. He turned to the girl and said:

"Honey, why don't you stop playing with the whistle for a bit and listen to me instead? You don't want to be too nosy, do you?"

The girl listened to her father and put the whistle away. From then on, Dug kept that lesson in mind - that being nosy isn't always the best thing to do. He was very happy he had taken the time to listen to the whistle and to his father's words.

Anna and Ben were best friends. They liked to play near the river. One day, they found a big raft made of wood and rope. They wanted to go on the raft and see the fish and the ducks.

"Can we go on the raft, please?" Anna asked Ben.

"I don't know," Ben said. "The raft does not belong to us. Maybe someone else needs it."

"But it looks so fun," Anna said. "And we are very careful. We will not break it or lose it."

Ben thought for a moment. He was an intelligent boy. He had an idea.

"OK, we can go on the raft, but only for a little while," he said. "And we have to ask the owner first. Maybe we can find him or her."

Anna agreed. They looked around and saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a hat and a fishing rod.

"Excuse me, sir," Ben said. "Is this your raft?"

The man looked at them and smiled.

"No, it is not mine," he said. "I found it here this morning. I think it belongs to the river. It is a gift from nature."

"Wow, really?" Anna said. "That is so cool."

"Can we use it, please?" Ben said. "We want to see the fish and the ducks. We will be very careful and bring it back."

The man nodded.

"Sure, you can use it," he said. "But be safe and don't go too far. The river can be fast and tricky. And wear these vests. They will help you float if you fall in the water."

He gave them two vests and helped them get on the raft. Anna and Ben thanked him and pushed the raft into the water. They had a lot of fun on the raft. They saw many fish and ducks and waved to the man on the bench. They felt happy and free on the raft that belonged to the river.

One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, you can't play in the garden today. It is too wet and cold. You will get sick and dirty. You can play inside with your toys."

Lily was sad. She did not want to play inside. She wanted to play in the garden. She said, "But mom, I love the garden. Please, can I play in the garden?"

"No, Lily, you can't. I'm sorry, but it is not safe. Maybe tomorrow, if the sun comes out, you can play in the garden. Now, come inside and have some milk and cookies."

Lily did not listen. She was angry and stubborn. She ran out of the door and into the garden. She did not care if it was wet and cold. She wanted to have fun.

But soon, Lily realized that playing in the garden was not fun at all. The flowers were droopy, the butterflies were gone and the dirt was sticky. She slipped and fell in a puddle. She got mud all over her clothes and hair. She started to shiver and sneeze. She felt miserable.

She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had played inside. She wished she had some milk and cookies. She cried and cried.

Her mom heard her cry and came out to the garden. She saw Lily in the puddle, covered in mud. She felt sorry for her. She said, "Oh, Lily, what have you done? You are wet and dirty and sick. You did not obey me. You did not allow me to help you. Come on, let's go inside and get you cleaned up."

She picked up Lily and carried her inside. She gave her a warm bath, a dry dress and a cozy blanket. She gave her some milk and cookies and a hug. She said, "Lily, I love you. I only want what is best for you. Next time, please listen to me. I know what is good for you."

Lily felt ashamed and sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you too. You are right. I should have listened to you. I should have allowed you to help me. Thank you for taking care of me. Can I play in the garden tomorrow?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, you can play in the garden tomorrow. If the sun comes out and the garden is dry and bright. But only if you promise to be careful and follow my rules."

Lily nodded and said, "I promise, mom. I will be careful and follow your rules. I will be a good girl."

Mom kissed her and said, "That's my Lily. Now, let's read a story and have a nap. You need to rest and get well."

Lily snuggled with her mom and said, "OK, mom. I like stories and naps. I like you and the garden. I am happy."

The end.

The moral of the story is: Don't be a bully. Be kind and share. You can be strong and brave, but also nice and fun. You can roar, but also hug. You can be friends with your brother.

He grabbed the cake with his mouth. He ran away with it. Ben and Lily stopped fighting. They saw their cake was gone. They said, "Oh no! Where is our cake?"

They heard Spot barking outside. They ran to the door. They saw Spot eating their cake. He had split it with his teeth. He had crumbs all over his face. He looked happy. Ben and Lily looked sad. They said, "Oh no! Spot took our cake. He did not share it with us."

Their mom came to the door. She saw what happened. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben and Lily. You lost your cake. You were too busy splitting it and fighting over it. You did not enjoy it or share it. You learned a hard lesson. Sometimes, splitting is not good. Sometimes, sharing is better."

Ben and Lily nodded. They felt sorry. They hugged each other. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We're sorry, Spot. We were silly. We will share better next time." Their mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Ben and Lily. I'm proud of you. I have a surprise for you. I have another cake in the fridge. You can have it tomorrow. But only if you promise to share it nicely." Ben and Lily said, "We promise, mom. We promise." They thanked their mom. They thanked Spot. They went to bed happy. They learned to share.

They heard a noise in the tree. They looked up and saw a furry animal with a long tail. It was a squirrel. The squirrel was holding a nut in its mouth. It looked at Sara and Ben with big eyes.

"Hello, squirrel!" Sara said. She waved at the squirrel. "Do you want to play with us?"

The squirrel was shy. It did not want to play with Sara and Ben. It wanted to keep its nut. It ran to another branch and hid behind some leaves.

"Come on, squirrel, don't be shy!" Ben said. He tried to climb the tree. He wanted to see the squirrel better.

"Be careful, Ben!" Sara said. She did not want Ben to fall. She stayed on the ground and watched Ben.

The squirrel did not like Ben climbing the tree. It felt scared. It wanted Ben to go away. It threw its nut at Ben. The nut hit Ben on the head.

"Ow!" Ben said. He rubbed his head. He looked at the nut on the ground. He saw that it was not a real nut. It was a plastic nut. The squirrel had tricked him.

"Ha ha, squirrel, you are funny!" Sara said. She laughed at the squirrel. She picked up the plastic nut and held it up. She wanted to display it to the squirrel. "Look, squirrel, we have your nut!"

The squirrel did not think it was funny. It was angry. It wanted its nut back. It made a loud noise and showed its teeth. It wanted to scare Sara and Ben.

"Uh oh, squirrel, you are angry!" Ben said. He climbed down the tree. He did not want to make the squirrel more angry. He joined Sara on the ground. "Let's go, Sara, the squirrel does not want to play with us."

"OK, Ben, let's go," Sara said. She put the plastic nut back on the ground. She did not want to keep the squirrel's nut. She wanted to be nice to the squirrel. "Bye, squirrel, sorry for bothering you!"

Sara and Ben ran away from the tree. They looked for another place to play. They hoped to find some real nuts.

The squirrel watched them go. It was glad that they left. It came out of its hiding place. It picked up its plastic nut. It liked its plastic nut. It was its favorite toy. It put it back in its mouth and ran to another tree. It hoped to find some more nuts.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play in the forest. They were not afraid of anything, not even the big wolf who lived there. They thought the wolf was funny and friendly, and they often gave him some of their food.

One day, they found a big basket of cookies and pies in the forest. They were very hungry and wanted to eat them all. But the wolf came and said, "Hello, little ones. Can I have some of your food? I am very hungry too."

Lila and Ben did not want to share. They said, "No, wolf. These are our food. You can find your own food. Go away!"

The wolf was sad and angry. He said, "That is not nice. You should share with others who need help. If you do not share, I will order you to give me your food. And if you do not obey, I will eat you!"

Lila and Ben laughed. They said, "You cannot order us. You are not our boss. And you cannot eat us. You are too old and slow. We are faster and smarter. You are a disgusting wolf. Go away!"

The wolf was very sad and angry. He said, "You are very rude and mean. You will see what happens when you do not share and respect others. I will teach you a lesson."

The wolf waited until Lila and Ben were busy eating the cookies and pies. Then he sneaked behind them and grabbed them by their clothes. He dragged them to his cave and locked them inside. He said, "Now you will stay here until you learn to share and respect others. And maybe I will eat you later."

Lila and Ben were very scared and sorry. They said, "Please, wolf, let us go. We are sorry for being rude and mean. We will share with you and respect you. Please, wolf, forgive us."

The wolf said, "I will think about it. But first, you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will never be rude and mean to anyone again. And you have to promise me that you will always share and respect others. Do you promise?"

Lila and Ben said, "Yes, wolf, we promise. We promise with all our heart. Please, wolf, let us go."

The wolf said, "OK, I will let you go. But you have to keep your promise. And you have to give me some of your food. And you have to be my friends. Do you agree?"

Lila and Ben said, "Yes, wolf, we agree. We will give you some of our food. And we will be your friends. Thank you, wolf, for being kind and forgiving."

The wolf said, "You are welcome, little ones. Come, let us eat together and be friends."

The wolf opened the cave and let Lila and Ben out. They gave him some of their cookies and pies, and they ate together and talked. They became friends and learned to share and respect each other. They never forgot the lesson that the wolf taught them.

The moral of the story is: You should share and respect others who need help. You should not be rude and mean to anyone. You should not judge others by their appearance. You should be kind and forgiving. You should make friends with different kinds of people.

But then, she heard a loud honk and felt a warm wing around her. It was her mama! Her mama had followed her and scared the bear away. She hugged Pippa and said, "Pippa, I am so glad you are safe. But you should never ignore me again. I only want to protect you and love you."

Pippa felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, mama. I was wrong. I wanted to be adventurous, but I did not think of the danger. I love you too, mama. Can we go home now?"

Her mama smiled and said, "Yes, Pippa, we can go home. But first, let me show you something. Look over there." She pointed to the other side of the hill, where the sun was setting and making the ice sparkle. "This is a beautiful sight, but it is not worth risking your life. You can be adventurous, but you also need to be careful and listen to me. Do you understand?"

Pippa nodded and said, "I understand, mama. Thank you for saving me and showing me this. You are the best mama in the world."

They cuddled and watched the sun go down. Then, they slid and waddled back to their home, where the other penguins welcomed them. Pippa learned her lesson and never ignored her mama again. She still liked to explore, but she always asked her mama first and stayed close to her. She was happy and safe, and so was her mama.

Sam was a regular boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a lot of cars, trucks, and trains, but his favorite toy was a red horn. He liked to blow the horn and make loud noises. He thought it was fun and funny.

One day, Sam went to the park with his mom and his horn. He saw some other kids playing on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. He wanted to join them, but he was shy. He did not know how to make friends. He thought maybe his horn could help him.

He ran to the swings and blew his horn as loud as he could. The other kids looked at him and frowned. They did not like the noise. They told him to go away. Sam felt sad and ran to the slide. He blew his horn again, hoping to make them laugh. But they did not laugh. They got angry and told him to stop. Sam felt sadder and ran to the sandbox. He blew his horn one more time, wishing to make them like him. But they did not like him. They threw sand at him and told him to leave. Sam felt very sad and ran to his mom.

His mom saw him crying and hugged him. She asked him what was wrong. Sam told her that he wanted to play with the other kids, but they did not like his horn. They did not want to be his friends. His mom said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I know you love your horn, but not everyone likes loud noises. Maybe you should try something else to make friends. Do you know what I recommend?"

Sam shook his head. He did not know what to do. His mom said, "I recommend that you use your words. Words are better than horns. Words can say hello, how are you, what is your name, do you want to play. Words can be kind, polite, and friendly. Words can make friends. Why don't you try that?"

Sam nodded. He wiped his tears and put his horn away. He took a deep breath and walked to the swings. He saw a girl with a yellow dress and a blue hat. He said, "Hello, I'm Sam. What is your name?" The girl smiled and said, "I'm Lily. Nice to meet you, Sam." Sam smiled back and said, "Do you want to play?" Lily said, "Sure, let's play." They played on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. They had fun and laughed. They became friends.

Sam was happy. He learned that words were better than horns. He thanked his mom for her recommendation. He still liked his horn, but he only used it at home. He used his words at the park. He made more friends and had more fun. He was a regular boy who liked to play with his toys and his friends.

"I'm building a shelter, Lily," her dad replied. "It will keep us safe if it rains or storms."

Lily was excited to have a new shelter, but she was also worried. "Daddy, will we still be rich when we have a shelter?" she asked. 

Her dad smiled and said, "We may not be rich in money, but we have each other and that's all that matters." 

Lily felt better and helped her dad finish building the shelter. They sat inside and enjoyed the cozy space together. From then on, Lily knew that having a shelter and a loving family was all she needed to be happy.

Once there was a small caterpillar. He was very hungry and wanted to find some food. He walked around and around, looking for something to eat, but he could not find anything.

Suddenly, he spotted a tall tree. He scuttled over to it and climbed up to the top. From the top, he saw a garden with lots of delicious food. He measured the distance from the tree to the garden with his tiny legs.

The caterpillar was so hungry, but he couldn't find a way to get to the garden. He looked around and spotted a long stick lying in the grass. He measured the stick and thought it just might be long enough for him to bridge the gap between the tree and the garden.

He crawled over to the stick and used it to climb down to the garden. Once he was in the garden, he started eating all the tasty food. He ate so much that he didn't have room for anymore!

He felt so happy and satisfied that he thought it was the best measuring stick he had ever used.

In the end, Tim decided to listen to his mom and not eat the cake. He went back home and told his mom about the cake. She was very happy that Tim listened to her warning. They both went back to the cake and shared it with their friends.

The moral value of the story is to always listen to the warnings given by our loved ones, as they want the best for us.

Lily realized that the frog must have been under a spell. She knew she had to help him. She searched the stream for something that could break the spell. Finally, she found a shiny stone that she thought might work. She held it up to the frog and said, "Abracadabra!" Suddenly, the frog grew back to his normal size.
