One morning he spotted a huge tomato. He smiled and started to slip towards it, but he was too excited and he slipped over. He began to cry - the huge tomato was ruined!

"It's ok, my little one," his mum said. "Let's go get another tomato".

So the little boy and his mum went to find another tomato, but none were as big or as yummy as the huge one. They had to go home empty handed.

The little boy was so sad. He had wanted that huge tomato so badly. He didn't like the ending at all.

Once upon a time, there was a pup named Max. Max was a small pup but he was very persistent. He always wanted to find something to do, but one day nothing seemed to keep him interested. He began to get frustrated and decided to take a walk.

As he meandered around the town, he came across a collar that was very shiny. Without a second thought, he stole the collar and kept it to himself. He was very proud of himself that he managed to steal the collar.

Max was now so proud of his collar that he wore it everywhere. Even when he went to bed at night, he wore his special collar. But one day, his family noticed the collar around Max's neck and knew he had stolen it.

Luckily for Max, his family was very understanding and persistent. They tried to talk to him and explain why stealing was wrong. Max was very sorry and gave the collar back to its rightful owner.

Max learned a valuable lesson that day - being persistent and doing the right thing is more important than stealing. He never stole again and his collar was returned to its rightful owner.

One day, a little girl was mailing something. She put her mail in the box and stepped back to admire it. Suddenly, a snake slithered out of the box! The snake was elderly, so he moved very slowly.

The girl was scared, so she ran into the house. Inside, she found her grandma. She explained everything to her grandma, and her grandma knew just what to do.

Grandma walked out to the mailbox with a bowl of food. She set it near the snake. The elderly snake was very hungry, and started eating.

Grandma then took the snake far away from the house, down the street, and placed him in a forest so he could live safely.

The little girl smiled. Even though the snake had scared her at first, she had looked after it and given it a new home. She knew it was safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had an old napkin that he always carried with him. His mom would always tell him to throw it away, but he loved it too much to let it go.

One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. They decided to play hide and seek. Timmy found a really good hiding spot behind a tree. But when he peeked out from behind the tree, he saw that his old napkin had fallen out of his pocket.

One of his friends saw the napkin and said, "Ew, that napkin is so old and dirty!" Timmy felt sad and embarrassed. But then another friend said, "It doesn't matter if it's old or dirty, it's still Timmy's favorite napkin."

Timmy felt happy again and realized that it's okay to love something even if it's old or dirty. He learned that true friends don't care about those things and that it's important to be kind to others.

Tom was a boy who liked to make noise. He had a toy drum, a toy guitar and a toy trumpet. He played them all day and all night. His mom and dad did not like the noise. They said, "Tom, please play quietly. You are making our ears hurt."

One day, Tom saw a big brown dog in the park. The dog was barking loudly. Tom thought the dog was funny. He wanted to play with the dog. He ran to the dog with his toy trumpet. He blew the trumpet in the dog's face. The dog did not like the trumpet. The dog growled and showed his teeth.

"Tom, stop that! You are making the dog angry!" his mom shouted. But Tom did not listen. He blew the trumpet louder and louder. The dog barked louder and louder. The dog jumped at Tom and bit his trumpet. The trumpet broke in half. Tom was scared and sad. He dropped the trumpet and ran to his mom.

"Mom, the dog broke my trumpet!" he cried.

"I'm sorry, Tom, but you should have listened to me. You made the dog angry with your noise. You need to be careful and respectful of animals. Maybe next time you will play quietly," his mom said.

Tom nodded. He hugged his mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you."

He learned his lesson. He never played his trumpet near a dog again. He still liked to make noise, but he managed to play quietly when he had to. He was a good boy.

Lily and Ben liked to play with blocks. They could build many things with blocks. They could build houses, towers, bridges, and cars. Sometimes they shared their blocks, and sometimes they wanted their own blocks.

One day, Lily had an idea. She wanted to build a bathtub with blocks. She thought it would be fun to pretend to take a bath with her dolls. She asked Ben, "Can I have some of your blocks? I want to build a bathtub."

Ben looked at his blocks. He was building a car with his blocks. He liked his car. He did not want to give his blocks to Lily. He said, "No, these are my blocks. You have your own blocks. Go build something else."

Lily felt sad. She did not have enough blocks to build a bathtub. She said, "Please, Ben, can I have some of your blocks? Just a few. I will give them back to you when I am done."

Ben shook his head. He said, "No, no, no. These are my blocks. Go away, Lily."

Lily started to cry. She did not like Ben. She thought he was mean. She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Ben is not being very nice. He should share his blocks with you. But you know what? You can be patient. Maybe he will change his mind later. Or maybe you can find something else to build a bathtub with. Do you want to look for something else?"

Lily nodded. She wiped her tears and said, "Yes, mom. I want to look for something else. Thank you, mom."

Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good girl. You are patient and creative. I love you, Lily."

Lily said, "I love you too, mom." She gave her mom a kiss and went to look for something else to build a bathtub with. She found some cardboard boxes, some tape, and some paper. She thought they would make a good bathtub. She worked hard and made a bathtub with them. She was happy. She put her dolls in the bathtub and pretended to wash them. She had fun. She did not need Ben's blocks. She was proud of her bathtub. She was patient and creative.

Once upon a time there was a modern farm with lots of hay. Every day the farmer set the hay to dry in the sun. One day, when the farmer was setting the hay in a big pile, a gust of wind blew through and scattered the hay far and wide. The farmer was so upset! He had tried to be so careful and now he had to redo all his hard work. But the farmer was determined to set the hay back where it belonged. 
He went to each location where the hay was scattered and set them all back into a big pile. After a lot of hard work he was finally finished. He was relieved and happy to have all the hay back where it belonged. 
The farmer was proud of his hard work and thanked the wind for helping him. From then on, the farmer made sure to set the hay on windy days- just in case.

Tim asked his friend, Sam, "Do you want to play hockey with me?" Sam said, "Yes, but we must return the hockey stick if we find the owner." Tim and Sam played and had lots of fun. But Tim did not want to return the hockey stick.

Later, an old man came to the park. He was very sad. He said, "I lost my hockey stick. Did you see it?" Tim hid the hockey stick and said, "No, I did not see it." The old man walked away, still sad.

Sam was mad at Tim. He said, "You are naughty! We should return the hockey stick to the old man." But Tim did not listen. He kept the hockey stick and played with it all day. The old man never found his hockey stick and stayed sad. Tim's friends did not want to play with him anymore because he was naughty.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah who really wanted to win.
She asked her mom, "Can I win?"
Her mom said, "Yes, Sarah. You can win at lots of things."

So Sarah decided to go to the park. But when she got there, she saw lots of other children playing games.
She wanted to join in, but she didn't know how.

Just then, she noticed a well in the middle of the park.
All around it, people were throwing balls into the well.
Sarah was excited. She had heard about a famous game called "Well Game."

She asked the other kids, "Can I play too?"
They said, "Yes! Everyone's welcome!"
So Sarah got to work and threw the ball into the well.

Sarah kept throwing the ball and before she knew it, she had won the game!
Everyone cheered for Sarah and she was so happy. From then on, she was known as the famous Well Game winner.

Once upon a time, there was a messy room. In the room, there was a big bookcase with many books. A little boy named Tim lived in the house. Tim loved to read books. He would take a book from the bookcase and read it every day.

One day, Tim's mom told him to clean his messy room. Tim did not want to clean. He wanted to read a book. So, he took a book from the bookcase and started to read. While he was reading, he felt a pinch on his hand. It was a tiny bug. The bug said, "Please clean your room, Tim."

Tim was very surprised. He listened to the bug and started to clean his room. He put all his books back on the bookcase. He picked up his toys and put them away. When he was done, his room was not messy anymore. The bug was happy and did not pinch Tim again.

The moral of the story is to always listen to your mom and keep your room clean.

Once upon a time, in a distant land, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to twist and turn when he danced. One day, Tim went for a walk in the woods. He saw a big tree with lots of ash around it. He wondered, "Why is there ash here?"

A small bird flew down and said, "Hi, Tim! The ash is here because there was a big fire a long time ago." Tim was sad to hear that, but he wanted to help. So, he got an idea. He asked the bird, "Can I dance to make the tree feel better?"

The bird smiled and said, "Yes, Tim! Your dance will make the tree happy." Tim started to twist and turn. He danced and danced. The tree began to grow new leaves and flowers. The ash went away, and the woods became beautiful again. Tim and the bird were very happy, and they danced together all day long.

Sara liked to balance on the big log in the park. She pretended she was a tightrope walker in the circus. She wore a red hat and a blue dress and smiled at the birds and the flowers.

One day, a mean witch came to the park. She saw Sara balancing on the log and she did not like it. She wanted to make Sara fall and hurt herself. She hid behind a tree and waited for the right moment.

"Hello, little girl," the witch said, coming out of the tree. "What are you doing on that log?"

"I'm balancing," Sara said, not noticing the witch's green skin and pointy nose. "I'm a tightrope walker. Do you want to try?"

"No, thank you," the witch said, pretending to be nice. "But I have a gift for you. A pretty necklace. Do you want it?"

Sara loved necklaces. She nodded and reached out her hand. The witch gave her a necklace with a big pendant. Sara put it on and thanked the witch.

But the necklace was not a gift. It was a curse. As soon as Sara wore it, she felt dizzy and heavy. She could not balance on the log anymore. She wobbled and stumbled and fell to the ground.

"Ha ha ha!" the witch laughed. "Now you will never balance again. You will be clumsy and weak and sad. That's what you get for being happy and brave."

Sara cried and cried. She wanted to take off the necklace, but it was stuck. She felt hopeless and scared.

But then, she heard a voice. A familiar voice. A friendly voice.

"Sara, Sara, where are you?" It was her big brother, Tom. He had come to the park to play with her. He had seen the witch and the necklace and he knew what to do.

He ran to Sara and hugged her. He took out a pair of scissors and cut the necklace off. He threw it away and said, "Don't worry, Sara. I'm here. You're safe. The witch can't hurt you anymore."

Sara felt better. She smiled and thanked Tom. She got up and said, "Let's go back to the log. I want to balance again."

Tom nodded and said, "Sure. Let's go. You're the best tightrope walker I know."

They held hands and walked to the log. The witch was gone. The birds and the flowers cheered. Sara balanced on the log and Tom clapped. They were happy and brave. The end.

Sam was a big boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many cars, trains, and planes that he could zoom around the floor. He also had a little sister, Lily, who was only two years old. Lily wanted to play with Sam's toys too, but Sam did not like to share. He said, "No, Lily, these are mine! Go away!"

Lily felt sad and miserable. She did not have many toys of her own, and she wanted to have fun with Sam. She tried to grab a car from Sam, but he pushed her away. Lily cried and ran to Mommy. Mommy hugged Lily and said, "What's wrong, sweetie?"

"Sam is mean! He won't let me play with his toys!" Lily sobbed.

Mommy frowned and said, "That's not nice, Sam. You should share with your sister. She is little and she wants to learn from you. You can teach her how to play with your toys, and you can have more fun together."

Sam did not want to listen to Mommy. He said, "But I don't want to teach her! She will break my toys! She doesn't know how to play right!"

Mommy said, "Sam, you were little once too. You did not know how to play with your toys until someone taught you. Remember how Daddy taught you how to make a train track? Or how Grandma taught you how to fly a plane? You were happy and proud when you learned something new. Don't you want Lily to feel the same way?"

Sam thought about what Mommy said. He remembered how much he liked to learn from Daddy and Grandma. He looked at Lily, who was still crying. He felt sorry for her. He said, "Okay, Mommy. I will teach Lily how to play with my toys. Maybe she can be my friend."

Mommy smiled and said, "That's very kind of you, Sam. I'm sure Lily will be happy to play with you. Come on, let's go and join her."

Sam and Mommy went to Lily and gave her a hug. Sam said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I will share with you. Do you want to play with my cars?"

Lily stopped crying and nodded. She said, "Yes, please, Sam. Thank you. Can you teach me how to zoom them?"

Sam said, "Sure, Lily. I will teach you. It's easy and fun. Watch me."

Sam and Lily started to play with the cars. They zoomed them around the floor, making noises and laughing. Mommy watched them and smiled. She was glad that Sam and Lily learned to share and teach each other. She thought, "They are good children. They will grow up to be good friends."

One day, a boy named Tom went to the beach with his mom and dad. He liked to play in the sand and look for shells and rocks. He saw a big brown octopus on the shore. It was not moving. Tom wanted to touch it.

"Mom, can I touch the octopus?" he asked.

"No, Tom, you can't. It might be sick or hurt. It might bite you. Leave it alone," his mom said.

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the octopus and lay down next to it. He reached out his hand and poked it. The octopus opened its eyes and wrapped its arms around Tom. It squeezed him hard. Tom screamed and cried.

"Help, help, the octopus is hurting me!" he shouted.

His mom and dad heard him and ran to him. They pulled the octopus off him and threw it back into the water. They hugged Tom and checked him for wounds. He had some red marks on his skin, but he was not bleeding.

"Tom, you are very lucky. The octopus could have hurt you more. Why did you not listen to me?" his mom asked.

"I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to touch the octopus. I did not know it was angry," Tom said.

"Tom, you have to listen to your mom and dad. They know what is best for you. They want to keep you safe. You have to be careful and respectful of the animals. They have feelings too. They do not like to be bothered or hurt. Do you understand?" his dad said.

"Yes, dad. I understand. I will listen to you and mom. I will not touch the octopus or any other animal without your permission. I learned my lesson," Tom said.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents and respect the animals.

Sara and Ben were playing in the farm. They liked to see the animals and hear their sounds. Sara liked the cow best. She wanted to pet it and feed it grass. Ben liked the horse best. He wanted to ride it and run fast.

They saw the cow in the field. Sara ran to it and said, "Hello, cow! You are so big and soft. Can I pet you?" The cow looked at her and mooed. Sara smiled and reached out her hand.

Ben followed her and said, "No, Sara! The cow is boring. Come and see the horse. It is so strong and fast. We can ride it and have fun." He pulled her arm and tried to make her go.

Sara did not want to go. She said, "No, Ben! The cow is nice. I want to stay with it. You can go and see the horse if you want." She pulled her arm back and stayed with the cow.

Ben was angry. He said, "Fine! I will go and see the horse. You are silly. The cow is not fun. It only eats and sleeps." He stomped away and left Sara alone.

Sara sighed. She did not like to fight with Ben. She liked him, but she also liked the cow. She wished they could play together and be happy. She hugged the cow and said, "Don't worry, cow. You are fun to me. Maybe Ben will come back and say sorry." The cow mooed and licked her face. Sara giggled and felt better.

One day, a little boy named Ben saw a big dragon in the sky. He was not afraid, he was curious. He wanted to talk to the dragon and make friends.

"Hello, dragon!" he shouted. "Can you come down and play with me?"

The dragon heard the boy and flew down to the ground. He was a friendly dragon, but he was also ignorant. He did not know much about people and their things.

"Hello, little one," he said. "What do you want to play?"

Ben smiled and pointed to his toy car. "This is my car. It can go fast and make noises. Do you want to try?"

The dragon nodded and picked up the car with his claws. He tried to make it go, but he did not know how. He pushed it, he pulled it, he shook it, but nothing happened. He got frustrated and angry.

"This car is broken!" he roared. "It does not work!"

He threw the car away and it landed on a rock. It broke into pieces. Ben was sad and angry too.

"No, dragon, no!" he cried. "You broke my car! You are ignorant! You do not know how to play!"

The dragon felt sorry and ashamed. He did not mean to break the car. He did not know it was important to the boy.

"I am sorry, little one," he said. "I did not know. I am ignorant. I do not know much about your things. But I can provide something else for you. I can provide fire."

He opened his mouth and breathed out a stream of fire. He made shapes and patterns with the fire in the air. He made a circle, a star, a heart, and a smiley face. He hoped the boy would like it.

Ben watched the fire and forgot about his car. He was amazed and happy. He liked the fire. He liked the dragon.

"Wow, dragon, wow!" he exclaimed. "You can provide fire! That is amazing! You are not ignorant, you are smart! You know how to make fire!"

He clapped his hands and laughed. He ran to the dragon and hugged his neck. The dragon hugged him back with his wings. They became friends. They played with fire and had fun.

Timmy was happy and got his journal and crayons. They drew pictures of their favorite animals and played together. Timmy's mom came outside and saw how happy Timmy was. She allowed him to draw outside from then on. Timmy was so happy he gave Billy a big hug. The end.

"Because we can play a game with them," Lily says. "We can pretend they are jewels and we are pirates."

"Thank you, Ben. You are very kind," Lily says. "Let's play pirates then."

They climb down the tree. They take their basket of cherries and run to the sandbox. They dig a hole and bury some cherries. They make a map and mark the spot. They pretend they are sailing on a ship and looking for treasure. They have a lot of fun. They are happy.

Tom nods and picks up a plastic ball. He puts it in a metal barrel that they use as a cannon. He aims at the birdhouse and says "Boom!"

But the ball does not fly very far. It falls on the ground and rolls away. Sam is angry and scolds Tom.

"Tom, you are a bad mate! You can't shoot the cannon right! You have to push harder and aim better!" Sam says. He takes the ball from Tom and tries to do it himself.

Sam and Tom drop the ball and the barrel and run to the house. They are scared and sorry. They did not mean to break the window. They just wanted to play pirates. They hope their mom is not too mad at them.

"Mommy, what does 'dry' mean?" Lily asked. 

"It means there hasn't been any rain in a long time, and the ground is very thirsty," her mommy explained. 

Lily was sad she couldn't play outside, but she had an idea. She filled up a bucket of water and poured it on the ground. The result was amazing - the grass turned green and the flowers started to bloom. 

From that day on, whenever it was too dry outside, Lily would water the plants and make everything beautiful again. And every time she did, she would smile and remember the day she questioned what "dry" meant, and the wonderful result that came from it.

Spot was happy too. He loved Sara. He said, "Woof, woof, love you, love you!" He did not mind being purple. He liked to be independent. He liked to be Sara's friend. He liked to mix things with Sara.

Once upon a time, there was a busy squirrel. It was so busy, it was always dashing around. One day, it came across a large store. It wanted to go inside, so it scampered up the stairs and through the door.

When it was inside the store, the squirrel looked around. There were many shelves filled with so many things! The squirrel explored the store and eventually found some delicious nuts. With a handful of treats, the squirrel left the store.

On its way out, the squirrel saw a little girl. She said, "Hello, squirrel! Where are you going with all those nuts?" The squirrel replied, "I'm storing them. I found them in the store and I'm taking them home for later." The girl smiled and said, "That's mighty busy of you, squirrel! I'm glad you found something yummy." The squirrel thanked the girl and scampered away with its stash.

From then on, the busy squirrel made sure to always keep some nuts stored away.

Once upon a time there was a barrel full of ice cream. It was big and juicy and very yummy! Everyone kept laughing and giggling as they ate it.

But then one day, a fierce tiger came running by. He wanted the ice cream too! He sped up to the barrel, but it was too heavy for him to move. So he left with a growl.

But then the people had an idea. They pushed the barrel as fast as they could and it went rolling across the ground. Everyone cheered as the barrel sped away!

They didn't know where the barrel was going, but it went so fast that it bounced up and down and around.

After a while the barrel stopped and the people laughed when they saw it. It was in front of the tiger!

The fierce tiger roared, but the people held the barrel tight and the tiger couldn't take it away. He was so mad he ran away.

The people were so happy they kept eating the ice cream. And they were thankful that the barrel was safe!

Anna and Ben are going to visit Grandma and Grandpa. They have to pack their bags. Anna likes to pack her books. She has many books. She likes to read and look at the pictures.

"Anna, are you ready?" Mom asks.

"Yes, Mom. I packed my books," Anna says.

Mom looks at Anna's bag. It is very heavy. Mom opens the bag. She sees many books. Some books are dirty. They have stains and tears.

"Anna, why did you pack so many books? And why are some books dirty?" Mom asks.

"I like books, Mom. I want to read them with Grandma and Grandpa. And some books are dirty because I read them a lot. They are my favorite books," Anna says.

Mom smiles. She understands. She loves books too. But she knows that Anna cannot take all the books. They will not fit in the car.

"Anna, I know you like books. But you cannot pack all of them. You have to choose some books. And you have to clean the dirty books. You want to show Grandma and Grandpa your nice books, right?" Mom says.

Anna nods. She knows Mom is right. She takes out some books from her bag. She keeps the ones she likes the most. She wipes the dirty books with a cloth. She puts them back in her bag.

"Good job, Anna. Now your bag is lighter and your books are cleaner. Grandma and Grandpa will be happy to see your books," Mom says.

"Thank you, Mom. I love you," Anna says.

"I love you too, Anna. Now let's go. Ben is waiting for us. He packed his toys," Mom says.

Anna and Mom go to the car. Ben is there. He has a bag with his toys. He likes to play with his toys. He packed his cars and his trains and his blocks.

"Hi, Anna. Hi, Mom. Are you ready?" Ben asks.

"Yes, we are ready. We packed our books and our toys. We are going to have fun with Grandma and Grandpa," Anna says.

"Yes, we are. Let's go," Ben says.

Mom drives the car. Anna and Ben sit in the back. They hold their bags. They are happy. They are going to visit Grandma and Grandpa.

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, big and small, with different clothes and hair. She liked to pretend they were her friends and have tea parties with them. One day, she found a new doll in her room. It was very pretty, with a pink dress and curly hair. Lily wanted to play with it, but it was too big for her table and chairs.

She asked her mom, "Can I make this doll smaller, mom? It does not fit with my other dolls."

Her mom said, "No, Lily, you cannot make the doll smaller. It is a regular doll, not a magic doll. If you try to shrink it, you might break it or hurt it. Why don't you play with it on the floor or on the bed?"

Lily was sad. She wanted to have a tea party with all her dolls, not just some of them. She thought of a plan. She took the new doll to the bathroom and put it in the sink. She turned on the hot water and let it run over the doll. She hoped the hot water would make the doll shrink. She also used a soap and a sponge to rub the doll all over. She thought the soap and the sponge would help the doll shrink too.

She waited for a few minutes, then turned off the water and took out the doll. She was shocked. The doll did not shrink. It was still the same size. But it looked very different. The pink dress was faded and wrinkled. The curly hair was tangled and matted. The doll's face was smudged and dirty. The doll looked very sad and ugly.

Lily felt very bad. She realized she had made a big mistake. She had not shrunk the doll, she had ruined it. She started to cry. She ran to her mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom, I'm sorry. I tried to shrink the doll, but I made it worse. I don't want this doll anymore. I want a regular doll, like my other dolls."

Her mom hugged her and said, "Oh, Lily, what have you done? You should have listened to me. You cannot shrink a regular doll. You can only love it and take care of it. This doll was a gift from your grandma. She made it for you with her own hands. She wanted you to have a special doll, different from your other dolls. She wanted you to be happy."

Lily felt even worse. She did not know her grandma had made the doll for her. She did not know it was a special doll. She wished she had not tried to shrink it. She wished she had loved it and taken care of it. She said, "I'm sorry, mom, I'm sorry. I'm sorry, grandma, I'm sorry. Can we fix the doll, mom? Can we make it pretty again?"

Her mom said, "I don't know, Lily. It might be hard to fix the doll. But we can try. Maybe we can wash it and dry it and comb it and sew it. Maybe we can make it look better. But it will never be the same as before. It will always have some marks and scars from what you did. You have to learn to accept it and love it as it is. And you have to promise me you will never try to shrink a regular doll again."

Lily nodded and said, "I promise, mom, I promise. I will never try to shrink a regular doll again. I will accept it and love it as it is. I will be nice to it and play with it. I will have tea parties with it and my other dolls. I will say sorry to it and thank you to grandma. I will be a good girl, mom, I will."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily, that's good. I love you, Lily, and so does grandma. And so does the doll, I'm sure. Come on, let's go and try to fix the doll. Maybe we can make it happy again."

As he walked closer, he heard a loud noise. It sounded like two of his friends, Susie the koala and Sammy the squirrel, were discussing something. When he finally got close enough, he saw that they were standing in front of an enormous green door.

Blue was curious, so he decided to join them. Susie and Sammy discussed the door and wondered where it led. They shared their speculation with Blue and he was also eager to find out. With a little bit of encouragement, Blue made up his mind and opened the door.

To his surprise, Blue found a huge, green garden full of fruits, vegetables and flowers. Blue was filled with excitement and he knew he had discovered something special.

The three friends spent the afternoon picking delicious fruits, playing games, and exploring the enormous green garden. From that day forward, Blue and his two friends would visit the garden often to discuss and enjoy all its wonders.

"Come back, balloon!" Sara cried. "We want to play with you!"

Ben was sad too. He wished they had not let go of the string. He hugged his sister and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. It was my fault. I should have held the string tighter."

Sara shook her head and said, "No, Ben. It was not your fault. It was the wind. The wind was too strong. We could not stop it."

They looked at each other and smiled. They knew they still had each other. They decided to go back inside and play with their toy planes. They learned that sometimes things can fly away, but they should not be sad. They should be happy for what they have.

The end.

Lily loved to read novels. She had many novels in her room. She liked to read them every day. She did not like to share her novels with anyone. She was selfish.

One day, her friend Ben came to play with her. Ben saw her novels and wanted to read one. He asked Lily, "Can I read one of your novels, please?"

Lily said, "No, they are mine. You cannot read them. Go away."

Ben was sad. He said, "But I like novels too. Why are you so selfish? Sharing is good. Don't you want to be my friend?"

Lily did not care. She said, "I don't need friends. I have my novels. They are more fun than you. Leave me alone."

Ben left. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. He hoped to find a better friend. A friend who was kind and generous. A friend who liked to share.

Lily stayed in her room. She read her novels. She was alone. She did not have any friends. She was not happy. She realized that she was wrong. She wished she had shared her novels with Ben. She wished she had been his friend. She hoped he would forgive her.

The moral of the story is: Don't be selfish. Share what you have with others. Friends are more important than things.

"Oh, Lila and Ben, you found our soda jug!" Mommy said. "It is not milk, it is soda. It has bubbles and gas in it. That is why it makes weird noises."

"Soda jug?" Lila and Ben asked. They had never seen soda before.

"Yes, soda jug. We bought it for a party. It is a special drink for grown-ups. It is not for toys or kids." Daddy said. He raised the jug and put it back on the shelf. He cleaned the floor with a cloth.

"Sorry, Mommy and Daddy. We did not know." Lila and Ben said.

Lila and Ben nodded. They hugged Mommy and Daddy and said sorry again. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with something else. They did not want to touch the weird soda jug again.

So, Lily and the bee worked hard to save the flower. They watered it and gave it some sunshine. After a few days, the flower was nice and healthy again. 

Lily: "Thank you so much for helping me, bee. You're a great friend."

Bee: "No problem, Lily. I'm always happy to help."

John and his family had a special day planned. They were going to go camping and have lots of fun. John couldn't wait! He loaded the car with all the camping supplies and away they went.

John and his family pitched the tent in a nice spot by a lake. John grabbed the hose and started to spray the tent to keep it cool. He loved the feeling of the water on his skin.

After they finished setting up the tent, they went to explore. John liked to find animals and plants but today he was feeling lazy. So he found a tree and just sat in the shade and watched the birds and bugs fly by. 

John's family went swimming in the lake. The sun was now getting ready to set. John joined them and they had a lot of fun splashing around in the water.

At the end of the day, John was tired and happy. He had started the day with a spray and now it was time to go to sleep with wonderful memories from the day.

Once upon a time, there was a big lake. In the lake, there lived a swan. The swan was very pretty with white feathers. One day, the swan felt thirsty and wanted to drink water from the lake. But the swan was anxious because there were other animals in the lake that might hurt it. 

The swan decided to wait until it was safe to drink. It watched the other animals carefully and when it saw that they were not going to harm it, the swan drank the water. The water was cool and refreshing. The swan felt happy and content. 

From that day on, the swan was not anxious anymore when it wanted to drink water. It knew that it just had to be patient and wait for the right moment. And so, the swan continued to live in the lake, swimming and enjoying the cool water every day.
